title: Stale Count in setInterval
description: This timer component is supposed to increment every second. In production, it increments to 1 on the first second, then freezes at 1 indefinitely. Spot the line containing the bug.
explanation: Line 8 captures `count` from the initial render closure (value: 0) because the dependency array on Line 11 is empty `[]`. In every tick, `setCount(0 + 1)` sets state to 1. Fix: Use functional updater `setCount((prev) => prev + 1)` or add `count` to the dependency array.

title: Missing Re-render on Array Push
description: Clicking the 'Add Item' button does not update the list on screen even though the console confirms the function ran. Spot the line that prevents React reconciliation.
explanation: Line 7 mutates the existing state array in-place. Because `items` reference does not change, `Object.is(items, items)` evaluates to `true` on Line 8, causing React to completely bail out of re-rendering. Fix: Create a new array instance via spread `[...items, newItem]`.

title: Unconditional State Setter in Effect
description: The browser tab freezes with 'Maximum update depth exceeded' error immediately upon mounting. Spot the line triggering the render loop.
explanation: Line 15 lists `status` in the dependency array. On Line 8 and Line 13, `setStatus` is called inside the effect. Updating `status` triggers the effect again, which calls `setStatus('loading')`, causing an infinite re-render loop. The dependency should only be `[userId]`.

title: Array.forEach with Async/Await
description: The function returns 'Processed all users' immediately before any database updates actually finish executing. Spot the line breaking the asynchronous flow.
codeLines: const record = await db.users.findByIdAndUpdate(id, { active: true });
explanation: Line 4 uses `Array.prototype.forEach`, which expects a synchronous callback and completely ignores the returned Promise from `async`. Execution flows straight to Line 9 while the promises are still pending in the microtask queue. Fix: Use a standard `for...of` loop or `await Promise.all(userIds.map(...))`.

title: Unbound Callback in Class Method
description: Calling `notifier.start()` throws 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' after 500ms. Spot the line causing the context loss.
explanation: Line 7 defines a regular `function() {}` callback. In non-strict mode or standard event loops, regular callbacks invoked by `setTimeout` execute with `this` bound to the global object (`window` or `undefined` in strict mode), losing the class instance context. Fix: Use an arrow function `() =>` or `.bind(this)`.

title: Numerical Array Sorting
description: The function returns `[10, 100, 2, 25, 5]` instead of `[2, 5, 10, 25, 100]`. Spot the line where the sorting logic fails.
fixedCode: const sorted = prices.slice().sort((a, b) => a - b);
explanation: Line 4 calls `.sort()` without a comparator function. JavaScript's `Array.prototype.sort()` converts elements to strings and compares UTF-16 code units lexicographically, so `'100'` comes before `'25'`. Fix: Provide a numeric comparator `(a, b) => a - b`.

title: Persistent State in Default List
description: Calling `append_log('User Login')` twice results in `['User Login', 'User Login']` on the second call even though no target list was passed! Spot the line defining the buggy default.
explanation: Line 3 uses a mutable list `tags=[]` as a default parameter. In Python, default parameter expressions are evaluated once when the function is defined, not when called. All subsequent invocations share the exact same list instance in memory. Fix: Use `tags=None` and initialize `if tags is None: tags = []`.

title: Skipped Elements in List Removal
description: The function is supposed to remove all even numbers from `[2, 4, 6, 8]`. Instead, it outputs `[4, 8]` because elements are skipped during iteration. Spot the faulty loop line.
explanation: Line 2 iterates over the original `numbers` list while Line 4 modifies its length in-place with `.remove()`. Removing an element shifts subsequent elements left by 1 index, causing the loop's internal index counter to skip the next adjacent element. Fix: Iterate over a shallow slice copy `for num in numbers[:]` or use a list comprehension.

title: z-index Ignored on Static Element
description: The dropdown menu is hidden behind adjacent sibling elements despite having `z-index: 9999`. Spot the line where positioning is missing or misconfigured.
explanation: Line 3 declares `z-index: 9999`, but according to CSS specifications, `z-index` only applies to positioned elements (i.e. `position` other than `static`, such as `relative`, `absolute`, or `fixed`), or flex/grid children. Without a positioned rule, `z-index` has zero effect.

title: Truncated Text Overflowing Flex Child
description: The text with `text-overflow: ellipsis` fails to truncate and expands the flex parent beyond the viewport width. Spot the line where flex minimum size is unconstrained.
explanation: Line 7 sets `flex: 1` on a flex child. By default, flex items have `min-width: auto`, which prevents the flex item from shrinking smaller than its content width. This overrides `text-overflow: ellipsis` and causes overflow. Fix: Add `min-width: 0;` to allow the child to shrink.

title: Error Handler Misidentified as Standard Middleware
description: When an error is thrown in a route, this custom error handler is completely bypassed, and Express falls back to its default HTML error page. Spot the faulty signature line.
codeLines: res.status(500).json({ success: false, message: 'Internal Server Error' });
explanation: Line 5 provides an error middleware with only 3 arguments `(req, res, next)`. Express checks `fn.length === 4` via function arity to identify error-handling middleware. Without the 4-argument signature `(err, req, res, next)`, Express treats it as regular middleware and skips it when `next(err)` is called.

title: ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT Crash
description: When an unauthenticated request arrives, the server crashes with 'Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot set headers after they are sent to the client'. Spot the line causing double response execution.
explanation: Line 3 sends a 401 response, but does not `return`. JavaScript execution continues sequentially to Line 6 and Line 7, attempting to send a second 200 response on the same HTTP socket, crashing the process with `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT`. Fix: Add `return res.status(401)...`.
